title: The common law tradition
summary: Common law is law developed through judicial decisions rather than enacted statutes. In England, King Henry II's Assize of Clarendon of 1166 ordered inquests in every county through twelve lawful men of each hundred. The English tradition later spread: early courts in the United States relied heavily on English common law before developing their own doctrines. Common law systems today include many political entities tied to the English tradition, where case law holds a pre-eminent place.
